title: National Assessment of Protection and Reintegration Needs, Services and Gaps for Survivors of Trafficking in Persons in Uzbekistan
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Project Context and Scope

The project “Strengthening Survivor-Centred Protection and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons in Uzbekistan”, funded by Sida and implemented by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in cooperation with national partners, aims to strengthen the national response to trafficking in persons, with particular emphasis on the identification, protection and sustainable reintegration of trafficking survivors.

Under Outcome 2: Enhanced survivor-centred protection and sustainable reintegration support for survivors of trafficking, the project seeks to strengthen the quality, accessibility and sustainability of protection and reintegration services for trafficking survivors, as well as the capacities of governmental and non-governmental service providers.

To establish an evidence base for further strengthening the protection and reintegration system, IOM will conduct a comprehensive national assessment combining three interrelated components: an assessment of the needs of trafficking survivors; mapping of existing protection and reintegration services; and analysis of service gaps, barriers to access and limitations in existing referral pathways.

The assessment will compare identified and reasonably assumed needs of trafficking survivors with the existing response in Uzbekistan and determine the extent to which available services are accessible and capable of meeting the corresponding needs, while identifying significant gaps and limitations in the existing system.

The findings will be used by IOM and national partners, in particular the National Agency for Social Protection under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the National Commission on Combating Trafficking in Persons and Decent Work, as an analytical basis for identifying priority areas for further improvement of protection and reintegration services. Given the available resources and project timeframe, only some of the identified needs and gaps may be addressed through subsequent project interventions; the assessment should therefore also provide a broader evidence base for longer-term planning and further development of the national protection and reintegration system.

Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing

Migrants Assistance and Protection Unit, IOM Uzbekistan, PX0735
Tasks to be performed under this contract:
Tasks to be performed under this contract – under the direct supervision of the National Project Officer (Protection) and overall coordination of the Chief of Mission (CoM)

The overall objective of this consultancy is to establish a comprehensive evidence base on the protection and reintegration needs of trafficking survivors in Uzbekistan, the existing services available to address these needs, their accessibility and capacity to provide an adequate response, and significant gaps, barriers and limitations in the existing protection and referral system, in order to inform subsequent prioritization and improvement of protection and reintegration services by IOM and national partners.

To complete the assignment, the Consultant will carry out the following tasks:

1. Review the applicable national and international protection and reintegration frameworks and available evidence related to trafficking in persons in Uzbekistan, including relevant national legislation, policies, institutional mandates and referral arrangements, as well as applicable international standards, principles and guidance on the protection and reintegration of trafficking survivors, together with existing assessments, administrative data, studies and other available sources.
2. Assess the protection and reintegration needs of trafficking survivors, taking into account different forms and circumstances of exploitation and relevant individual characteristics and vulnerabilities, including the specific needs of women, men and children. The assessment should consider both identified needs and reasonably assumed needs where available evidence indicates that a protection need may exist despite limited reported demand or service use.
3. Map existing protection and reintegration services potentially relevant to the identified needs of trafficking survivors, including services provided by government institutions, non-governmental organizations and other relevant service providers. The mapping should cover, as relevant, the type and purpose of the service, responsible provider, target groups and eligibility, geographic coverage, institutional arrangements and referral pathways.
4. Assess practical accessibility and adequacy of the mapped services, including whether eligible trafficking survivors can effectively reach and use the service and whether the existing response is reasonably capable of addressing the corresponding protection or reintegration need. Relevant access barriers may include, inter alia, eligibility restrictions, geographic limitations, information gaps, administrative or documentation requirements, referral practices, cost, language, gender- or age-related barriers and other practical constraints.
5. Identify significant gaps and limitations in service provision and referral pathways, including situations where a relevant service does not exist, is inaccessible to some groups of survivors, does not adequately respond to the identified need, or where weaknesses in information, coordination or referral prevent effective access to an otherwise available service.
6. Analyse and structure the identified needs and gaps according to their significance and implications for protection and sustainable reintegration, providing an evidence-based basis for subsequent prioritization by IOM and national partners.
7. Develop practical recommendations for further strengthening the protection and reintegration system, clearly distinguishing between gaps that may require improvement or adaptation of existing services, strengthened access or referral arrangements, and areas where additional or specialized responses may need to be considered. Recommendations should provide an analytical basis for subsequent decision-making and should not prescribe the specific interventions to be implemented under the project.

Methodological Guidance

The Consultant shall propose a detailed methodology for IOM review and approval prior to commencing the substantive assessment. The methodology should be proportionate to the scope of the assignment and combine qualitative and quantitative information, where available and relevant, using appropriate methods which may include surveys, interviews, consultations and other suitable data collection approaches.

The assessment should be guided by the following principles:

• Needs-based approach. Protection and reintegration services should be assessed in relation to the identified or reasonably assumed needs of trafficking survivors, rather than mapped as a stand-alone inventory of available services.
• Survivor-centred and rights-based approach. The assessment should take into account the rights, safety, dignity, individual circumstances and vulnerabilities of trafficking survivors and avoid approaches that may expose survivors to harm, re-traumatization, stigma or unnecessary disclosure of sensitive information.
• Gender- and age-sensitive analysis. Differences in protection and reintegration needs, access to services and barriers faced by women, men and children should be considered throughout the assessment. Particular attention should be given to whether existing services are appropriately adapted to the specific needs of children and other groups requiring specialized responses.
• Triangulation of information. Findings should, where feasible, be based on multiple sources, including desk review, available administrative and programme data, consultations with relevant government institutions, non-governmental organizations and other service providers, and appropriately designed consultations with trafficking survivors or other sources reflecting survivor experience.
• Practical accessibility. The existence of a service should not in itself be treated as evidence that the corresponding need is being met. The assessment should consider how access works in practice, including eligibility, awareness and availability of information, referral mechanisms, geographic accessibility and other relevant barriers.
• International standards and good practice. The assessment should use applicable international standards, principles and relevant guidance on the protection and reintegration of trafficking survivors as a reference point for assessing existing services, practices and identified gaps, while taking into account the national legal, institutional and operational context of Uzbekistan.
• Proportionate and sufficient analysis. For each issue examined, the depth of analysis and amount of data collected should be proportionate to the significance of the identified or potential protection and reintegration need and sufficient to support a reasoned conclusion on the existence, accessibility and ability of the existing response to address that need. More detailed analysis should be undertaken only where available information is insufficient or indicates a significant gap or barrier.
• Cautious interpretation of reported demand. Absence or low levels of recorded demand or service utilization should not, in themselves, be treated as evidence of the absence or limited significance of a corresponding need, without considering possible barriers related to identification, awareness, accessibility and referral.
• Value for money and use of existing systems. The analysis should distinguish between gaps that may require new or specialized responses and those that could potentially be addressed through better use, adaptation, accessibility or coordination of existing services and structures.

The indicative range of protection and reintegration services to be considered may include, but is not limited to: safe accommodation and shelter; immediate material assistance; health and mental health and psychosocial support; legal assistance; documentation and civil registration support; family tracing and reunification, where appropriate; return assistance; case management and referral; social support; education and skills development; employment, livelihood and economic reintegration support; and other services relevant to the protection and sustainable reintegration needs identified through the assessment.

The Consultant should determine the appropriate depth of analysis for individual service areas based on their relevance to identified or potential needs. Detailed information on service capacity, staffing, caseload, resources or other operational characteristics should be collected where it is necessary to assess whether the service can reasonably meet the corresponding need, rather than as a mandatory requirement for every mapped service.

Stakeholder Engagement and Sources of Information

The assessment should draw on relevant available information and consultations with key stakeholder categories, as appropriate to the methodology and subject to IOM approval, including:

• Government institutions and public service providers with mandates relevant to identification, protection, assistance and reintegration of trafficking survivors at national and sub-national levels;
• Non-governmental and civil society organizations, including organizations providing specialized or general services accessible to trafficking survivors;
• International organizations and development partners, where they provide relevant services, technical support, data or evidence on existing protection and reintegration responses;
• Other relevant service providers and professional actors, including providers of legal, health, psychosocial, social, educational, employment and livelihood-related assistance, where relevant to identified needs;
• Trafficking survivors and/or sources reflecting survivor experience, using appropriate, ethical and safe methods that minimize risks of re-traumatization, stigma, harm or unnecessary disclosure of sensitive personal information;
• Existing documentary and data sources, including relevant legislation and policies, administrative and programme data, previous assessments and research, service documentation, referral arrangements and other available evidence.

The selection of stakeholders and sources should be sufficiently broad to enable triangulation of findings and identification of differences between formal institutional arrangements and actual practice. The Consultant should not assume that relevant protection or reintegration services are limited to institutions or organizations formally designated as trafficking-specific service providers.
The primary intended users of the assessment are IOM, the National Agency for Social Protection under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan, and the National Commission on Combating Trafficking in Persons and Decent Work. Findings may also support other relevant government institutions, non-governmental organizations and service providers in strengthening protection and reintegration responses for trafficking survivors.

Performance indicators for the evaluation of results

Deliverable

Content

Timeline / working weeks

Payment %

Inception Report, Methodology and Workplan

• Detailed methodology and analytical framework
• Desk review and proposed data sources
• Proposed stakeholder categories and consultation approach
• Approach to survivor engagement and ethical safeguards
• Assessment criteria and applicable national and international reference standards for analysing needs, services, accessibility, adequacy and gaps
• Detailed workplan and timeline
• Proposed structure of the assessment report

Week 2

20%

Draft National Assessment Report

• Assessment of protection and reintegration needs of trafficking survivors
• Mapping of existing protection and reintegration services and providers
• Analysis of practical accessibility and adequacy of existing services, taking into account applicable national and international standards and guidance

• Analysis of referral pathways and institutional arrangements
• Identification and analysis of significant service gaps and access barriers
• Structured analysis of needs and gaps to support subsequent prioritization
• Preliminary recommendations for strengthening the protection and reintegration system

Week 12

45%

Final National Assessment Report

• Revised and finalized assessment incorporating IOM comments and, where required, additional validation or clarification of findings
• Final findings, conclusions and recommendations
• Clear distinction between evidence, identified gaps and areas requiring further assessment or action
• Executive summary and key findings for use with national partners
• Relevant tables, diagrams, charts and other visual representations of findings
• Final report and supporting materials submitted in editable format

Week 16

35%

Language requirements: Deliverables 1 and 2 shall be prepared and submitted in Russian. Deliverable 3 shall be submitted in final versions in Russian and English. The English version shall accurately reflect the content of the finalized and approved Russian-language report.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Advanced university degree in migration, social sciences, law, human rights, social protection, public policy, international development, or a related field.

  • At least five years of progressively responsible professional experience in research, assessment, programme analysis or policy work related to trafficking in persons, migrant protection, social protection, human rights or related areas.

  • Demonstrated experience in conducting needs assessments, service mapping, gap analysis or similar research involving vulnerable populations.

  • Good knowledge of trafficking in persons, survivor protection and reintegration, including survivor-centred, rights-based, gender-responsive and child-sensitive approaches.

  • Experience in applying qualitative and quantitative research methods, including desk review, stakeholder consultations, interviews and analysis of administrative or programme data.

  • Experience engaging with government institutions, civil society organizations and service providers; experience working directly with vulnerable populations, including trafficking survivors, is a strong asset.

  • Good understanding of the institutional and social protection context of Uzbekistan and relevant national protection and referral systems.

  • Strong analytical, drafting and communication skills, including the ability to synthesize information from multiple sources and present complex findings in a clear and practical manner.

  • Fluency in Russian and Uzbek is required for research, consultations and stakeholder engagement.

  • Strong command of English is required for preparation of the final English-language report.

Bidders are required to submit a separate financial proposal, including a detailed price schedule, as part of their application.

Languages

For this consultancy, Fluency in Russian and Uzbek, Strong command of English are required.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Travel required

The consultancy is home-based in Uzbekistan, and no travel is required by IOM under this assignment.
Should the Consultant consider travel within Uzbekistan necessary for the effective completion of the assignment, such travel shall be undertaken at the Consultant’s own expense. Any related costs shall be borne by the Consultant and, where applicable, reflected in the financial proposal. IOM will not provide separate reimbursement for travel, accommodation, daily subsistence allowance or other travel-related expenses.

Purpose of Assignment and Scope of the work

All work assignments under this contract shall take place on a home-based basis in Uzbekistan, and it will be assumed that the service provider holds the responsibility to ensure all necessary permissions to work in the country.

The materials produced under this assignment will be credited to IOM Uzbekistan. The Consultant will ensure that all deliverables are prepared and submitted in accordance with the language requirements specified under Section 7 and provided in editable digital format. All original materials, data and supporting documentation produced or collected under the assignment will be handed over to IOM Uzbekistan and will remain the property of IOM Uzbekistan.

Each work assignment shall be discussed in advance and an individual Purchase Order describing the nature of the job request, timeframe and budget shall be issued. Assignments will be requested and managed by the Migrants Assistance and Protection Unit of the IOM Country Office in Uzbekistan.
All copyrights to materials produced in the performance of this contract shall be vested exclusively in IOM Uzbekistan. Any use of such materials by the service provider shall be subject to the prior written consent of the IOM Uzbekistan Chief of Mission.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Notes

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

title: Senior Project Manager, DOE Construction Projects
description:
About Us

Every moment of every day, people all over the world rely on the infrastructure work provided by Quanta Services and Quanta Government Solutions (QGS). With its highly skilled and innovative workforce, Quanta is the largest specialty contractor in North America that powers modern life. Find your future with us by being a part of something bigger – leading the energy transition in building a better world for generations to come.

Imagine what you could do here. We encourage and inspire our people to embrace opportunities within our corporate office and 200 operating companies providing solutions for the utility, renewable energy, electric power, industrial, communications and government industries worldwide.

Quanta’s culture is about creating an environment where all employees can be themselves, are valued, and have an equal opportunity to succeed. When you join our team, you join a dynamic culture in which career development is encouraged, excellence is rewarded, and diversity is valued.

About this Role

COMPANY: Quanta Government Solutions

JOB TITLE: Senior Project Manager, DOE Construction Projects

DEPARTMENT: Construction Operations

LOCATION: Remote (Travel required to project sites)

REPORTS TO: Director of Construction Operations

MATRIX INTERFACES: Program Manager, Safety/Quality, Finance, HR, IT/Cyber, Legal/Compliance and Preconstruction.

CLASSIFICATION: Exempt

POSITION OVERVIEW

We are seeking an experienced and results-driven Construction Senior Project Manager to lead and execute QGS's most complex and strategically significant projects at DOE complexes. The ideal candidate will have a minimum of 10 years of DOE construction project management experience, to include Design-Build (DB) and Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) projects.

This role requires expert knowledge of construction trades, building regulations, federal compliance, project leadership and strong communication skills.

In addition to leading project execution teams, this role will require advising project management staff and contribute to the continuous improvement of project delivery processes across the organization.

The successful candidate will be accountable for delivering construction projects on time, within scope, and within budget while ensuring the highest standards of performance, client satisfaction, safety and quality.

What You'll Do

  • Project Leadership: Directs and leads QGS's most complex and significant DB/EPC DOE project teams from design to close-out, ensuring alignment with design goals and client expectations in real time.
  • Stakeholder Engagement: The position requires skills to be a trusted teammate and leader with DOE agencies, clients, subcontractors, consultants, and executive leadership to strengthen partnerships, resolve issues, and drive project success.
  • Budget & Resource Oversight: Provides strategic oversight of project estimating, budgets, forecasts, resource planning, material tracking, and financial performance across project portfolios.
  • Compliance & Risk Management: Ensures full compliance with DOE contract requirements (e.g., FAR and agency-specific regulations), proactively identifies enterprise-level risks, and implements mitigation strategies that protect project and organizational objectives.
  • Quality & Safety: Coordinated regularly with corporate and site-specific Quality and Safety Representatives to identify, track, report, and mitigate any potential quality and safety requirements or events.
  • Scheduling & Milestones: Provides executive oversight of project schedules and critical milestones, ensuring on time delivery while proactively recognizing and resolving complex schedule impacts.
  • Team Leadership: Leads, mentors, and develops Project Management staff and cross-functional project teams while building a culture of accountability, integrity, quality, and safety.
  • Reporting & Documentation: Provides executive-level project reporting, performance metrics, and strategic updates to clients and senior leadership, ensuring transparency, decision-making, and continuous improvement.

What You'll Bring

  • Experience: Minimum of 10 years managing construction projects on Municipal, State and Federal complexes. Specific experience at Department of Energy (DOE) sites with proven success leading high-risk and high-value construction projects. Proven ability to lead PM teams consistently and deliver successful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of positive communication, safety, quality, and client satisfaction.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in business, Engineering, Construction Management, or related field. Field trade experience, certifications and trades specific knowledge is a must.
  • Certifications: PMP, Six Sigma, OSH 15, OSHA 30, or other relevant PM and trade and software certifications preferred.
  • Regulatory Knowledge: Expert knowledge of federal DOE contracting procedures, compliance frameworks, procurement standards (FAR, ), and applicable industry regulations. Familiarity with NQA-1 quality standards preferred.
  • Technical Skills: Advanced proficiency with project management systems, scheduling, cost control, and reporting tools, including Procore, Microsoft Project, Primavera P6, and Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Soft Skills: Exceptional team leadership, negotiations, analytical, decision-making, and mentoring skills with a demonstrated commitment to servant leadership, safety, quality, and continuous improvement.
  • Communication: Builds strong rapport with clients and trades, connects in relatable, approachable manner across all organizational levels, demonstrates active listening and delivers clear, concise information, maintains transparent, timely feedback to ensure alignment and expectations.
  • Clearance: Current active or ability to obtain and maintain federal security clearance and satisfy project-specific background check requirements.

Preferred Licenses/Certifications

  • PMP
  • OSHA 30 Safety
  • Field Trade certifications
  • Construction Management Software

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Provides leadership, coaching, and mentoring to PM support staff and cross-functional project teams.
  • Supports staff development, workload balancing, and consistent project delivery within multiple projects.
  • Deliver clear, concise information, maintain communication, provide honest feedback to ensure expectations.
  • May need to provide input into performance evaluations, staffing, and succession planning.

TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS

  • Travel Required: Yes
  • Percent of Time: Up to 50%
  • Overnight Travel: Yes

  • Exposed to fumes or airborne particles - Seldom

Note: This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities, working conditions, physical demands, and activities my change or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice.

What You'll Get

Our Benefits & Perks

  • Company-paid life and disability insurance
  • Access to mental health support and resources
  • 160 hours of paid time off per calendar year, prorated in the year of hire based on the employee’s start date, along with 11 company-observed paid holidays

Growth & Development

title: ETCH Customer Engineer II
description:

We design, build and service cutting-edge equipment that helps our customers manufacture display and semiconductor chips – the brains of devices we use every day. As the foundation of the global electronics industry, Applied enables the exciting technologies that literally connect our world – like AI and IoT. Hiroshima,JPN

Your responsibilities include performing preventative and corrective maintenance on various systems such as electrical, vacuum, mechanical, plasma, hydraulic, and gas systems. title: Parent Advocate (Preventive Services)
description:
About the Role

Parent Advocates will support families involved with the child welfare/protective system at the time of their initial Child Safety Conference. Advocates will work closely with ACS, and Brooklyn and Queens-based organizations/ programs. Advocates, with their own personal prior lived experience of the child welfare system (qualifications below), will authentically and effectively inform and support parents; help to improve the sensitivity and practice of other child welfare professionals; and lead to positive and more equitable permanency outcomes for children and families. Parent Advocates help to ensure that parents understand their situation and options, the processes, roles, and responsibilities stakeholders/participants/involved parties, and promote effective communication and transparency. Advocates' primary involvement will be in the Initial Child Safety Conference, the start of the parent’s child welfare involvement, and will support parents, build a rapport, and help them navigate community resources and services.

The Parent Advocate will work primarily out of the ACS field offices with an expectation of some travel among the various field offices and Rising Ground Hubs.


What You’ll Do

  • Build rapport and support parents in coping with the trauma of child welfare/protective system involvement, making decisions for their families, and communicating effectively with those involved in their case.
  • Work with socially, economically, culturally, and ethnically diverse groups in a mutual respectful manner using a strength base and flexible approach.
  • Prepare parents and participate in Child Safety Conferences.
  • Emphasize with parents the importance of involvement in planning, preparing for court dates, voicing concerns, and requesting help when needed.
  • Collaborate with individuals in crisis to identify and or develop coping skills.
  • Report to the Advocate Supervisor and work collaboratively as part of interdisciplinary teams with ACS field offices staff and multiple community-based service providers.
  • Collaborate with other providers and community support to help families meet their needs and navigate resources.
  • Coach parents to strengthen problem-solving skills while discovering their strengths, hopes, dreams, and priorities.
  • Actively participate in team meetings, and supervisory sessions, including daily scheduling check-ins.
  • Maintain accurate job related/required reports and documentation and submit on a timely basis.
  • Complete assigned training as required.
  • Flexible Work Schedule
  • Perform all other related duties as assigned.


Your Qualifications

  • Minimum High School Diploma
  • Strong knowledge of community resources and services.
  • Warm, enthusiastic, and able to engage and positively impact individuals.
  • Someone who has a sincere appreciation for people and how they are each uniquely motivated.
  • Strong interpersonal skills to assist with parent engagement and are geared towards working sensitively on topics involving trauma, stress, and healing.
  • Good oral and writing skills.
  • Computer skills conducting Google searches and using Microsoft Office.
  • Skilled at working in a fast-paced environment on multiple projects occurring simultaneously.
  • Passion for parent leadership and preventing child welfare involvement.
  • Able to maintain a high level of confidentiality.

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

title: Composite Design Student Placement
description:
Red Bull Technology have an exciting opportunity for an Undergraduate Student to spend a year as part of our Composite Design department. The placement will run from summer of 2027 for one year and offer the chance to demonstrate your enthusiasm and apply your knowledge to real racing events!

Based on our Milton Keynes Campus this unique role covers a wide range of different technical areas, each demanding a high level of computer literacy and a clear understanding of the principles of mathematics, physics, and engineering. Interpersonal skills, good organisation, efficient and clear reporting will be equally valued.

Red Bull Technology is inviting candidates to apply for Industrial Placement positions within its Composite Design Department. Composite Design is fundamental to the creation of our F1 car. The chassis, impact structures, wings, bodywork are all composite assemblies, with far more to their design, manufacture & operation than might at first meet the eye!

Composite Design
The key accountabilities of this role are to:

  • Have an organised and methodical approach to your work.
  • Cover all aspects of Composite Design from clean sheet scheming/idea generation, tooling, detailed component design, assemblies, associated jigs, pit gear and supporting documentation.
  • Be involved in material selection, laminate design, structural sign off and fault fixing.
  • Show creativity, to suggest new ideas and concepts, and be involved in our wide ranging and ambitious composite R&D activity.
  • Be confident in presenting your ideas and design work.
  • Be prepared to be flexible to suit changing priorities and to go the extra mile as and when required.

Candidates wishing to apply for this role should demonstrate an active interest in Composite Design, be studying towards a mechanical/aeronautical engineering degree (or similar), be computer literate and prepared to carry out hands-on tasks.

To be eligible for this placement applicants must be returning to higher education to study for at least 1 year after their placement year.

Confirmation of this should be in place at time of application. While we would like to open this opportunity up to all applicants these positions are intended to be a work placement for students currently undertaking higher education and is therefore the eligibility requirement. Please do not apply if you do not fall within the requirements for this position.

The placement will be for 1 year, starting in the summer of 2027. To be considered for this Student Placement, please apply to this advert and submit both your CV and a one-page Cover Letter.

Not only is this a fantastic opportunity to complete your student placement at our championship winning team, but it is also a great opportunity to work with some of the greatest talents in F1. A good salary is just the start, there are many other benefits too, such as a free daily food allowance, free gym access and fitness classes, multiple discounts and offers with our partners, free barista style coffee, unlimited Red Bull and much more!

Application closing date: 16:00 (BST) Friday 25th September 2026.

title: Senior Construction Associate (Shelter)
description:
Since 2014, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in close partnership with the governments, United Nations (UN), and non-governmental organizations (NGOs), has been addressing a range of migration-related issues, including disaster risk management in Malawi in line with its strategic objective of “driving solutions to displacement”. IOM Malawi also supports the Government of Malawi to strengthen systems and capacity for disaster risk reduction and climate resilience with a focus on minimizing the risk of climate-induced displacement and improving the management of displacement at all levels.

The Regional Responses to Climate Displacements in Sub-Saharan Africa (RE2CLID) project aims to enhance the resilience and self-reliance of Displacement-Affected Communities (DACs) in Sub-Saharan Africa who face the risks of disasters, the adverse effects of climate change and environmental degradation. This initiative targets the highly vulnerable displacement affected communities in Southern Africa and the Indian Ocean Countries, namely Malawi, Mozambique, Madagascar, Comoros, Mauritius and Seychelles (i.e. Cluster 2).

Under the overall supervision of the RE2CLID Programme Coordinator in Malawi and direct supervision of the National Shelter Officer, and in collaboration with relevant units at IOM Malawi, the successful candidate will be responsible and accountable for providing technical assistance in planning, construction and rehabilitation of shelter and other infrastructure related to disaster risk reduction.

1. Support in planning and implementation of site assessment and site planning prior to construction of shelters and related infrastructure.
2. Support in the assessment including of existing shelters and infrastructure, or damage caused by the hazards or disasters to identify rehabilitation and maintenance needs.
3. Support the development of BOQ’s and designs for planned shelters and other infrastructures and facilitate approval of BOQs and designs.
4. Under the supervision of the National Shelter Officer, plan, coordinate and supervise construction activities (including supervising the deployed skilled, semi-skilled and unskilled labours) in selected sites to ensure timely completion of works.
5. Participate in meetings and conferences; maintain effective liaison and coordination with local authorities, partners, intergovernmental and non-governmental organizations and other stakeholders on matters related to shelter and infrastructure construction and management.
6. Support in the identification and documentation of good practices and lessons learned; contribute to the development of Standard Operations Procedures (SOP), and concept papers
7. Support in designing, planning and execution of technical trainings for artisans including identifying trainees and maintaining records of all training activities.
8. Perform other related duties as assigned.

EDUCATION
Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, Architecture and other engineering-related fields from an accredited academic institution with at least 5 years of relevant professional experience.

EXPERIENCE
1. Minimum of 5 years’ experience in site assessment, planning, and site layout for the purpose of shelter construction.
2. Minimum of 5 years’ experience in designing and supervising the construction of communal, transition and permanent shelters for internally displaced persons in accordance with the sphere standards and applicable Government guidelines.
3. Experience in working with migrants, refugees, internally displaced persons, victims of trafficking, and other vulnerable groups.
4. Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organizations in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.
5. Experience in training local artisans on Build Back Better and Safer technics.

SKILLS
1. Organizational skills and attributes:
-Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
-Ability to work with diverse stakeholders and facilitate collaboration.
-Ability to work in teams and collaborate to deliver outcomes.
-A good planner
2. Specific Skills:
-Training skills: Experience in developing training materials and conducting artisanal capacity building activities.
- Technical skills: Ability to work with AutoCAD and other computer-based design software.
- Report Writing and Analysis: Strong analytical and report-writing skills are essential.
-Adaptability and Flexibility: Ability to adapt to a dynamic environment and work under pressure.

title: Vehicle Suspension Design Student Placement
description:

  • Developing proficiency in specialist areas of CAD design, CAD draughting, engineering calculations, fault diagnosis and fixing, elementary stress analysis, elementary vehicle dynamics.
  • The preparation of technical documentation for the circuit.
  • Developing problem solving and communication skills through working closely with Designers, Aerodynamicists, Vehicle Dynamicists, Race Engineering, Mechanics, Manufacturing and technical specialists from throughout the organisation.
  • Following best practice as defined by the design manual for all activities.
  • Occasional travel on company business as requested.

The successful applicant will demonstrate:

  • An understanding of vehicle suspension, driver controls and braking systems.
  • An understanding of Mechanical Engineering principles and calculation.
  • A good understanding of a 3D CAD system and willingness to learn a new package.

To be eligible for this placement applicants must be returning to higher education to study for at least 1 year after their placement year. While we would like to open this opportunity up to all applicants these positions are intended to be a work placement for students currently undertaking higher education and is therefore the eligibility requirement.

Please do not apply if you do not fall within the requirements for this position.

The placement will be for 1 year, starting in the summer of 2027. To be considered for this Student Placement, please apply to this advert and submit both your CV and a one-page Cover Letter. Applicants demonstrating the necessary skills and experience will be invited to undertake a technical exam followed by an online interview for the final short-listed candidates.

Not only is this a fantastic opportunity to complete your student placement at our championship winning team, but it is also a great opportunity to work with some of the greatest talents in F1. A good salary is just the start, there are many other benefits too, such as a daily food allowance, free gym access and fitness classes, multiple discounts and offers with our partners, free coffee, unlimited Red Bull and much more!

title: Technical Trade Compliance Specialist (EMEA)  (m/f/d)
description:

What Will Make You Successful
You are able to bridge the gap between engineering, operations, and regulatory compliance.
You enjoy working with technical information and collaborating with engineers and business stakeholders to solve complex challenges.
  • Take ownership and drive initiatives independently.

  • Balance business objectives with compliance requirements.
  • Demonstrate strong attention to detail and sound judgment.

title: Vulnerability Analyst
description:
• The Endpoint Vulnerability Analyst supports endpoint vulnerability remediation efforts across enterprise endpoint environments. This role executes the vulnerability remediation lifecycle for assigned work—triage, risk-based prioritization, root-cause analysis, solution validation, deployment coordination, and reporting—partnering with security, operations, engineering, and application teams. The ideal candidate demonstrates endpoint technical depth, works independently on complex issues, contributes to automation and process improvements, and supports governance activities (SLAs, exception handling, and risk reporting) that improve the firm’s overall risk posture.
  • Key Responsibilities
  • Monitor and analyze endpoint vulnerability findings using Tenable/Nessus
  • Assess findings to determine business impact, root cause, and remediation requirements
  • Apply risk-based prioritization aligned to vulnerability severity, exploitability, asset criticality, and remediation SLAs
  • Coordinate endpoint remediation activities, including:
  • Windows and macOS updates and configuration changes
  • Patch management activities (OS and third-party applications)
  • Application and browser updates and configuration changes
  • Driver, firmware, and UEFI/BIOS updates
  • Removal, upgrade, or retirement of outdated applications
  • Develop, test, and troubleshoot PowerShell scripts to support remediation and automation
  • Partner with testing teams to validate remediation solutions prior to deployment
  • Create and manage ServiceNow incidents/requests and change records; support the change management process
  • Coordinate remediation execution with cross-functional teams (testing, deployment, operations, policy, and application owners)
  • Provide endpoint troubleshooting support related to vulnerabilities and remediation deployments
  • Facilitate meetings with internal teams (and business partners, as needed) to drive timely vulnerability resolution
  • Maintain remediation tracking data (task lists, status, owners, and timelines)
  • Prepare regular status reporting on remediation progress, exceptions, and outstanding risk
  • Support remediation exceptions and risk acceptance/waiver workflows; ensure documentation and approvals meet governance requirements
  • Produce and communicate vulnerability remediation metrics (e.g., aging, SLA attainment, recurrence) and provide insights to support decision-making
  • Prioritize and manage multiple concurrent remediation efforts in a deadline-driven environment
  • Follow established security, operational, and documentation standards; document work performed and outcomes
  • Build strong working relationships with partner teams to ensure consistent remediation outcomes
  • Identify recurring remediation gaps and contribute to process improvements (standard operating procedures, playbooks, automation) to reduce repeat vulnerabilities
  • Required Skills
  • 5+ years of experience in endpoint engineering/operations, vulnerability management, patch management, or a closely related discipline
  • Experience supporting Windows and macOS endpoints in an enterprise environment
  • Experience with vulnerability scanning and reporting tools (e.g., Tenable/Nessus)
  • Experience with endpoint security, patching, or vulnerability remediation processes
  • PowerShell scripting skills (writing, testing, troubleshooting, or modifying scripts)
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 tools (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) for tracking and communication
  • Experience using ServiceNow for ticketing and change management
  • Experience with remote support and troubleshooting tools (BeyondTrust preferred)
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Intune (device management and policy)
  • Additional Required Qualifications
  • Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional partners and drive work to completion without direct authority
  • Demonstrated organization and time-management skills
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results with minimal supervision
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including status reporting
  • Ability to partner with technical and non-technical stakeholders to drive outcomes
  • Growth mindset with a willingness to learn new tools, technologies, and security practices
  • Preferred Qualifications
  • Relevant certifications (e.g., Security+, CISSP, GIAC) and/or ITIL foundation

title: Bar Supervisor
description:

We’re seeking a passionate and experienced Bar Supervisor to join our existing leadership team and lead from the front — actively working behind the bar while guiding the team to deliver warm, seamless and elevated service.

You will be the lead bartender during service, driving drink quality, efficiency, stock management and cocktail training, while supporting the Shift Leader and Bar Manager. We promote a culture of trust, support, and acceptance. Always welcoming different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist

Your role

  • Deliver expert psychiatric care to patients across inpatient, outpatient and hospital-in-the-home services
  • Provide professional leadership within a well-resourced multidisciplinary mental health team

  • Work across a genuine breadth of clinical presentations in a supportive regional environment
  • Positions available at Senior Staff Specialist, Staff Specialist, or Senior Medical Officer level, dependent on experience and qualifications

What's on offer

  • Total remuneration package up to AUD $564,548 p.a.

title: Student Success Center Officer
description:

title: Lead Test Engineer
description:

title: Verkoopmedewerker Arnhem
description:
Word jij onze nieuwe Apple-expert?

Apple begint bij Amac! Bij Amac begin je zonder ervaring op de winkelvloer en groei je supersnel door tot Apple-expert. Je leert het vak van collega's, van Apple zelf en via de Amac Academy. Na een paar maanden geef jij zelf al advies waar klanten wat aan hebben.

Dit ga je doen

Je staat midden in de winkel en bent het eerste aanspreekpunt voor klanten met vragen over hun iPhone, MacBook of iPad. Je luistert goed, denkt mee en helpt ze verder: van een simpel advies tot de verkoop van een nieuw Apple-product. Geen dag is hetzelfde, dus je leert supersnel bij.

• Je geeft klanten advies dat klopt, zonder ingewikkeld gedoe.

• Je luistert naar wat iemand nodig heeft en denkt gewoon even mee.

• Je leert het vak via trainingen, van je collega's en door het simpelweg te doen.

• Je deelt wat je leert met je team, want samen worden jullie beter.

• Je houdt de winkel netjes en verzorgd.

• Je viert het als het goed gaat: blije klanten, mooie verkoopcijfers, een team dat scoort!

Waarom je hier wilt beginnen

• Je krijgt betaalde trainingen van Apple en de Amac Academy, en bouwt kennis op waar je je hele leven wat aan hebt.

• Je groeit snel door: naar floormanager, specialist of een andere rol binnen Amac.

• Je werkt elke dag met de nieuwste Apple-producten, vaak nog voordat iedereen ze kan kopen.

• Je maakt deel uit van een hecht team, met teamuitjes en gezellige avonden samen.

• 25 vakantiedagen op fulltime basis.

• Personeelskorting op producten in onze winkels en kans op leuke teamprijzen.

• €2.350 tot €2.500 per maand op fulltime basis, en dat groeit mee zodra jij doorgroeit.

Net klaar met school of al even op zoek naar een baan die echt bij je past: bij Amac mag je gewoon beginnen en jezelf zijn.

Herken jij jezelf hierin?

• Je bent sociaal en durft op mensen af te stappen.

• Je vindt technologie vet en wil er meer over leren.

• Je blijft rustig als het druk is en houdt het leuk.

• Je bent flexibel beschikbaar (20–36 uur per week).

• Ervaring met klantcontact is een pluspunt, maar geen must. Belangrijker is dat je sociaal bent, graag leert en energie krijgt van het helpen van klanten.


Wat kan je verwachten nadat je hebt gesolliciteerd?

  1. Je solliciteert in een paar minuten en je hoort binnen enkele werkdagen van ons.

  2. Klinkt het goed? Dan plannen we een kennismakingsgesprek in de winkel, zodat je meteen voelt hoe het is om hier te werken.

  3. Klikt het van twee kanten? Dan volgt een tweede gesprek of een korte meeloopdag op de vloer.

  4. Match gevonden? Dan krijg je ons aanbod en verwelkomen we je in het team.


We houden het proces kort en persoonlijk: je weet snel waar je aan toe bent.

title: Adviserend Verkoopmedewerker

Met jouw persoonlijke aanpak draag je dus elke dag bij aan een positieve verandering! Dit doe je vanuit één van onze mooie winkels in de gezelligste steden van Nederland.

Groei uit tot de expert in vitamines en supplementen! Als Adviserend Verkoopmedewerker krijg je alle ruimte om je kennis te vergroten. Dankzij de support van ervaren collega’s en gerichte scholing sta jij elke dag sterker in je schoenen.

Naast het geven van persoonlijk advies, draag je ook bij aan de bijbehorende winkelwerkzaamheden als het aanvullen van producten, verwerken van bestellingen, het draaien van de kassa en het netjes presenteren van producten in de winkel.

Wie zijn wij?

De Vitaminstore onderscheidt zich al ruim 28 jaar met een sterk merk, een ruim assortiment en deskundig- en persoonlijk advies. Wij geloven dat gezonde voeding en natuurlijke verzorging bijdragen aan een duurzame wereld, waarin mensen zich fysiek en mentaal goed voelen. Wat bieden wij?

Pyeongtaek-Mokok,KOR

As a Field Service Engineer [Customer Engineer] at Applied Materials, you serve as the direct liaison with customers, collaborating closely to install, maintain, and upgrade equipment. Your responsibilities include performing preventative and corrective maintenance on various systems such as electrical, vacuum, mechanical, plasma, hydraulic, and gas systems.   • Install, maintain, and upgrade customer equipment

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Completion of an Associate degree, military technical training, field service experience, or trade certification

  • 4-7 years of work experience in semiconductor industry or other equipment support industry

Assignee / Regular

Yes, 20% of the Time

No

title: Senior Red Team Specialist
description:
Your opportunity:

As a Senior Red Team Specialist, you'll work in close collaboration with our Blue Team, emulating real-world threat scenarios to assess and improve our overall security posture. Unlike a traditional penetration tester, your role extends beyond identifying system vulnerabilities. Instead, you'll imitate genuine tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) used by potential threat actors relevant to our operations.

Our environment is as diverse as it is innovative, requiring a creative and adaptive mindset. From our 5G radio networks to our eCommerce platforms and warehouse systems, you'll navigate a range of technologies and environments. Success in our Red Team means adapting traditional attack techniques to fit this diverse landscape while emulating our threat actors.

You'll make impact by:

  • Maintain an in-depth understanding of TPG Telecom's offerings, our operations, and potential attack vectors.
  • Propose, plan, and execute red teaming operations to emulate realistic threats to our organisation, including threats specific to telecommunication systems.
  • Automate attack techniques and create custom tooling for specific operations, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and innovation.
  • Write great reports detailing the objectives and outcomes of Red Team operations, including observations and recommendations for improvement.
  • Collaborate with our Security Incident Response Team to enhance detection and response capabilities.
  • Work closely with our Infrastructure Security Team to propose defensive improvements across our varied environments, including our mobile networks and cloud systems.
  • Work alongside non-technical teams to propose enhancements and additions to existing policies and processes.
  • Take part in our gamified collaboration exercises.
  • Stay informed on current security trends, advisories, publications, and academic research relevant to our organisation and the broader telecommunications industry.

What you’ll bring:

  • Experience in cybersecurity roles such as Red Team Specialist, Ethical Hacker, Security Consultant, Penetration Tester, or similar.
  • In-depth understanding of the MITRE ATT&CK framework with the ability to utilise threat intelligence to create relevant Red Team scenarios.
  • Proficiency in scripting and programming languages like Python, Go, and Ruby to automate tasks and create custom security tools.
  • Command-line experience with Linux-based operating systems
  • Experience exploiting vulnerabilities in web applications, cloud environments Linux and/or MacOS workstations, and software supply chains.
  • Strong understanding of telecommunications systems, including familiarity with RF (Radio Frequency) concepts, wireless network architectures, and mobile communication standards like 4G, and 5G.
  • Experience with field-based and hands-on technical tasks within safety regulations.
  • Proficiency in a range of security testing tools and methodologies.
  • Hands-on experience with at least one of the major cloud providers.
  • An adversarial mindset with the ability to think like an attacker.
  • Excellent and professional communication skills (written and verbal) with an ability to articulate complex topics in a clear and concise manner.

Ideally, you will also have:

Relevant qualifications which are desired but not required are:

  • CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional)
  • OSEP (Offensive Security Experienced Penetration Tester Certification)
  • OSCP (Offensive Security Certified Professional)
  • PNPT (Practical Network Penetration Tester)
  • eCPPTv2 (eLearnSecurity Certified Professional Penetration Tester)

What's in it for you?

  • Flexible hybrid way of working (from home and office)
  • ‘Stay Connected Mobile’ – Access to a free mobile plan
  • ‘Stay Connected NBN’ – Access to a free, high‑speed NBN plan (up to 500 Mbps)
  • ‘Your Leave’ - additional leave to be used whenever you like - every year
  • Access to TPG Learning Hub platform and internal development opportunities
  • Access to Corporate Partner Discounts

Don’t meet every single requirement? That’s OK! At TPG Telecom, we’re all about creating an accessible workplace where everybody feels safe to bring their authentic self to work - regardless of background. If you think this role is a great fit for you but some of the qualifications don’t align with your experience, we still encourage you to apply - you might just be the perfect candidate for a similar role with us!
