title: Expedited SVN: Field Security Officer (P)
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

This is an expedited recruitment process, open for applications from internal and internal-equivalent candidates only.

Organizational Context and Scope

The Office of Staff Security (OSS) is responsible for providing leadership on security policy management and Country Office operational support to enable effective implementation and delivery of IOM programmes and activities, while managing security risks at acceptable levels.

Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (COM) and under the technical supervision of the Office of Staff Security (OSS) as represented by the Regional Security Officer (RSO) based in the Regional Office in Cairo, the Field Security Officer will be responsible and accountable for providing expert support to enable IOM’s activities in the Country Office with all aspects of security risk management.

The Field Security Officer will be expected to implement appropriate safety and security management procedures that will effectively address issues that could and have impact on the security of IOM personnel, premises, assets, and operational activities.

1. Establish and maintain effective working relationships with security officials of other United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS) organizations, government counterparts and partner security services, country United Nations Department Safety and Security (UNDSS) office and all appropriate Security Focal Points, in order to obtain up-to-date security-related information that is beneficial to the Country Office.

2. Provide accurate and up to date assessments of the security situation in the Country Office and provide advice and recommendations to the COM/ Head of Office (HoO) on how to prevent and mitigate against identified threats and risks.

3. Develop, implement, and regularly test a functioning warden system. Warden testing methods should include multiple systems, including SCAAN.

4. In coordination with the RSO, COM /HoO, prepare Country-specific training activities, seminars, briefings, coordinate staff participation, and ensure that security training is carried out professionally within IOM and UNSMS learning/training standards.

5. Provide security briefings for IOM personnel deployed to and travelling within Yemen and coordinate all travel security requirements for the Country Office relating to all IOM operations, including assessments of road, air and river transport networks, medical evacuations and international staff travel within and from/to Yemen.

6. In coordination with the RSO, regularly review and monitor compliance on the UN Security Risk Management Measures (SRMM) and Residential Security Measures (RSM). This includes proactively participating in the Security Cell Meetings and actively providing guidance to the COM/HoO on issues raised in the Security Management Team (SMT), ensuring that IOM-specific operational requirements are considered for implementation of security measures and that a people-centred approach is mainstreamed in security risk management.

7. Acquire comprehensive operational understanding of IOM programmes in the Yemen and provide recommendation, including Security Risk assessments in areas where IOM works or is planning to deploy its teams.

8. Support the COM/HoO by providing security-related inputs into the Country Office’s Business Continuity Plan, proactively advising the COM/HoO in its regular testing.

9. In coordination with the RSO, develop, implement and test Country Office-specific security plans.

10. Supervise Senior Security Assistants to ensure that the appropriate level of security is provided to IOM personnel.
11. Closely monitor and report on deployment numbers (staff ceilings) established for the mission/s by the UN Designated Official (DO) during emergencies, in coordination with the and UNDSS, ensuring that security clearance procedures are applied fairly, vis-à-vis all of the agencies working under the UNDSS Security Management System.

12. Test the functionally and implementation of IOM-specific emergency communications systems, including SCAAN to ensure they are functional, effective and address the programme requirements of the Country Office. This includes actively checking the SCAAN dashboard and posting relevant security advisories in a timely manner.

13. Report security matters that have a potential or direct impact on IOM operations immediately to the COM and the RSO.

14. In coordination with the COM and the RSO, conduct preliminary enquiries in respect to any security breaches/incidents in the Country Office, working closely with local authorities in efforts to ensure IOM personnel, its assets and interests are protected and appropriate and corrective measure taken.

15. Perform such other duties as maybe assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Master’s degree in Security Management, Business Administration, Political/Social Science, Psychology, Criminal Justice, Law, International Relations or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
  • University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.
  • Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Experience in international relations, disarmament affairs, conflict resolution, crime or terrorism prevention, security, risk, disaster, or crisis/emergency management and preparedness in the public or private service areas, responsible for responding to emergency situations that may directly impact security is desirable;
  • Experience in planning, design, implementation or review of risk mitigation measures related to operations impacted by insecurity is desirable;
  • International experience is desirable;
  • Management experience in the humanitarian, public, private or corporate sector is desirable;
  • Minimum one year of experience in field operations is desirable; and,
  • Specialized experience in such areas as security programmes, risk assessments, or analysis is desirable.

Skills

  • UNDSS certification to any of the following: Security Certification Programme (SCP), Security Analysis Practice and Process (SAPP), Hostage Incident Management (HIM), Trainer Development and Certification Course (TDC) and Safe and Secure Approaches in Field Environments (SSAFE) is desirable;
  • Ability to collaborate with senior government security counterparts and relevant stakeholders is an advantage;
  • Demonstrated ability to manage a high degree of rational behaviour and decision making at all times;
  • Ability to supervise and work effectively with colleagues from varied cultures and professional backgrounds, and;
  • Excellent oral and written skills. Listens actively and responds effectively.

Languages

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Arabic and another official UN language (Chinese, French, Russian and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.
  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.
  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.
  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.
  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings.

Notes

Internationally recruited professional staff are required to be mobile. Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to all clearances, including medical and security as well as accreditation, any residency or visa requirements. Vacancies close at 23:59 local time Geneva, Switzerland on the respective closing date. No late applications will be accepted.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, harassment, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and any forms of discrimination. IOM is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children.

IOM conducts reference checks and background verification, including through system wide databases such as ClearCheck, to help ensure that candidates have no record of misconduct, including on sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, or fraud. Candidates are expected to uphold these standards and principles at all times.

title: Senior Python Data Scraping Engineer (Freelance)
description:
Mindrift is looking for highly skilled Vibecode specialists to join the Tendem project () and drive specialized data scraping workflows for real-world use cases. Mindrift is looking for highly skilled Senior Python Data Scraping Engineers to join the Tendem project and drive specialized data scraping workflows for real-world applications. In this role, you'll apply your expertise in web scraping, data extraction, and data processing to deliver accurate, reliable, and high-quality results. This part-time remote opportunity is ideal for technical professionals with hands-on experience in web scraping, data extraction and processing.

What We Do

The Mindrift platform connects specialists with innovative technology projects. Our mission is to help develop high-quality AI technologies by combining real-world expertise from professionals across the globe with advanced AI development efforts.

About the Role

This is a freelance role for a Tendem project. As a Senior Python Data Scraping Engineer, you'll handle data scraping tasks requiring technical precision for web extraction and processing, utilizing tools such as Apify, OpenRouter, and other technologies, alongside your own technical expertise and approaches.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end data extraction workflows across complex websites, ensuring complete coverage, accuracy, and reliable delivery of structured datasets.
  • Leverage available tools and custom workflows to accelerate data collection, validation, and task execution while meeting defined requirement.
  • Ensure reliable extraction from dynamic and interactive web sources, adapting approaches as needed to handle JavaScript-rendered content and changing site behavior.
  • Enforce data quality standards through validation checks, cross-source consistency controls, adherence to formatting specifications, and systematic verification prior to delivery.
  • Scale scraping operations for large datasets using efficient batching or parallelization, monitor failures, and maintain stability against minor site structure changes.

Educational qualifications

  • At least 5+ years of relevant experience in data engineering, web scraping, automation, or software development (required).
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, or related technical fields is a plus.

Academic and/or Professional Experience

Candidates should have a strong technical foundation and practical experience with scripting, automation, and data extraction workflows. We are looking for specialists who can solve non-trivial problems, work confidently with modern development tools and technologies, and systematically collect, structure, and validate data from diverse sources. A methodical, detail-oriented approach and the ability to work independently are essential.

Technical Skills (Essential)

  • Strong experience in Python web scraping (BeautifulSoup, Selenium or similar), including dynamic content (JS, AJAX, infinite scroll) and APIs via proxies
  • Proven ability to extract data from complex structures (hierarchies, archived pages, inconsistent HTML)
  • Solid background in data cleaning, normalization, and validation, delivering structured datasets (CSV, JSON, Google Sheets)

Additional requirements

  • Demonstrated experience handling anti-bot mechanisms and dynamic site structures at scale
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS or equivalent) and containerization (Docker) as part of real workflows
  • Hands-on experience with LLM frameworks (LangChain, OpenRouter, or similar) applied to automation tasks
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy
  • Self-directed work ethic with ability to troubleshoot independently
  • A link to GitHub is a plus
  • English proficiency: Upper-intermediate (B2) or above (required)

Project time expectations

For this project, tasks are estimated to require around 10–20 hours per week during active phases, based on project requirements. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed workload, and applies only while the project is active.

Compensation

On this project, contributors can earn up to $30 per hour equivalent, depending on their level and pace of contribution. Compensation varies across projects depending on scope, complexity, and required expertise. Please note that other projects on the platform may offer different earning levels based on their requirements.

title: Assistant Community School Director Bronx
description:
ABOUT US

New York Edge is the largest provider of after-school and summer camp programs in New York City public schools. Each year, academic programs—including STEM, the arts, sports and wellness, and college access—help 40,000 students develop leadership skills and succeed in school. Working parents count on our programs to provide safe and enriching environments for their children.


Summary:

New York Edge is looking for a Community School Assistant Director to assist with establishing a high and visible presence within the school building supporting the Community School Director in assuming a strong leadership role and holistic approach toward improving academic performances driven by strong, collaborative partnerships among principals, parents, teachers, and CBO’s throughout the school year. The Community Schools Assistant Director will assist in the overall administration and implementation of the Community Schools program under the supervision of the Community School Director including but not limited to: trainings, theme based projects, scheduling of activities, daily supervision of staff, record keeping and reporting, communicating with parents and organizing special events. The Assistant Director will work with the Community School Director in ensuring all components of the contract are being implemented in alignment with the vision of New York Edge and the Principal. New York Edge Assistant Director must embrace positive school climate and youth development principles and practices that supports the community school as a whole. These include building on youth strengths rather than focusing on youth deficits; setting and maintaining high expectations; understanding the centrality of and fostering positive relationships with peers and adults; providing age-appropriate and challenging programming; engaging participants as partners, not just as consumers of services; promoting positive identity formation and helping young people to fully develop their potential. New York Edge Community School Assistant Director respects and values the cultures and traditions of participants, their families and their communities, and treats all participants and staff equally, irrespective of race, religion, sex, gender identity, national origin, age or disability. New York Edge Program Coordinator must appreciate the range of abilities and diverse needs of children and youth in our programs.

Essential Job Functions:

  • Work hand-in-hand with Community School Director in daily program operations and functions
  • Work with school leadership to maintain a focus on results and track progress. Ensure that New York Edge is capturing, and analyzing data while functioning in a data driven manner.
  • Directly responsible for overall supervision of community school support specialists and success mentors’ for day school program.
  • Assist in the educational and social development of students under the direction and guidance of the facilitator and classroom teachers.
  • Ensures that they are trained in the methodology employed during the school day in regards to instruction
  • Encourage and lead projects that foster academic, cultural and artistic growth.
  • Provide support for individual students inside and outside the classroom to enable them to fully participate in activities.
  • Responsible for recruitment and supervision of dedicated staff that meet the highest standards of qualifications in carrying out the mission of Community Schools and New York Edge
  • In conjunction with academic support specialist, assesses student progress and communicates such to teachers and school administrators.
  • Works with academic support specialists and subject teachers to provide student support in various curriculum areas.
  • Must attend Professional Developments offered by New York Edge and Department of Education faculty.
  • Identify high need students, coordinate with teachers to target interventions, and track and monitor impact of interventions.
  • Build relationships and mechanisms to effectively link the school day to expanded learning opportunities
  • Communicate program’s challenges, progress and success with Program Director, will perform projects assigned at the discretion of the Program Director
  • Support students with emotional or behavior concerns and assist them in developing appropriate social skills.
  • Coordinate the allocation of space for student and family support services, and for special events.
  • He/she fosters an atmosphere of fun and learning and serves as a role model to youth, always conducting him/herself in the utmost professional manner and maintaining appropriate boundaries
  • Promotes positive character development in all youth
  • Participate in school governance, community school team meetings, and specialized meetings such as attendance meetings.

Interacts With:

Community School Director, Principal, Teachers, School Administrators, Vendors, Parents, Students

Required Skills:

  • Passion for New York Edge mission and youth development
  • Reliable, organized and punctual
  • Knowledge of effective sports, arts, and academic programming
  • Expert understanding of New York City and New York State education requirements in an urban setting
  • Strong leader and team-builder
  • Ability to resolve conflicts and negotiate solutions
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with program staff and school partners
  • Excellent communication (oral and written) and interpersonal skills with proven ability to interact with a diverse range of individuals both in person and over the phone, applying tact and discretion as situations demand
  • Must have excellent organizational, time management and follow-up skills
  • Must be able to clearly articulate outcome requirements and provide the necessary and appropriate resources and support for Academic Support Specialists, Teachers and Group Leaders to successfully deliver on objectives
  • Responsible and professional conduct that serves as role model to staff and youth
  • Exhibits strong character traits and exercises patience and creativity while seeking win-win scenarios
  • Ability to set priorities and meet deadlines
  • Must demonstrate ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Outlook, Google Docs, and Word

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree required with preference in Education, Psychology, or Social Work
  • At least 18.0 credit hours from an accredited college or university in the field of Education
  • Must have passion for New York Edge mission and demonstrated interest in the field of education and youth development.
  • Prior work experience in urban education, including supervisory experience
  • Teaching and afterschool management experience preferred


Job Type: Full-Time, Year-Round

Salary: $58,500

Schedule: Monday - Friday, (Some evenings & weekends required)



To apply, please visit our website at newyorkedge.org/careers

At time of offer and acceptance, the job requires safety and security clearances through the Department of Education and Department of Health.

New York Edge is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer.

title: Care Team Specialist
description:
Position Purpose:

Under direction of the Care Team Supervisor & Program Director, the Crisis Prevention Specialist/Care Team Specialist will be participating in a multi-disciplinary team, contributing to client engagement, retention, safety and support for the clients of the DTLA Cecil Hotel Interim Housing Program. The position will interact with staff and clients as a care team member by building rapport and fostering a sense of community.

The DTLA Cecil Hotel Interim Housing Program assists homeless, individuals to recover and improve their quality of life. These individuals may also suffer from mental health and substance abuse issues, sometimes causing behaviors such as yelling, cussing, and outbursts of anger. The role of each staff at JWCH is to assist the client in overcoming barriers and increasing coping skills to decrease negative behaviors and live in PSH successfully.

Principal Responsibilities:

  1. Establish a positive rapport with clients and express a concern for their well-being.
  2. Demonstrate understanding and practice harm reduction methods.
  3. Demonstrate understanding of trauma-informed care.
  4. Demonstrate non-violent restraint methods, if needed and only as an absolute last resort.
  5. Monitor the floors by walking corridors and perimeter of the building.
  6. Maintain a front desk sign in/out sheet for clients, as well as visitors.
  7. Search clients and/or visitors belongings when they enter the building.
  8. Assist with clients’ room searches and/or temperature control, as needed.
  9. Act as floor lead during fire drills and real emergencies, and as lead in performing necessary chair evacuations.
  10. Document any client and/or client-staff incidents and submit to supervisor in a timely manner.
  11. Answer front desk phone, as needed.
  12. Ability to follow all crisis protocol.
  13. Escort clients to appointments when needed.
  14. Use appropriate de-escalation techniques and seek assistance when required.
  15. Demonstrate understanding and awareness of substance abuse and/or negative behavioral health symptoms.
  16. Must be able to work extended shifts when emergency situations warrant in a 24 hour 7 day a week setting.
  17. Flexibility to adjust with a multiple schedule change, shift change, and days off. Work schedule is subject to change periodically based on the number of Care Team Specialists.
  18. Provide supportive communication on incarceration, substance abuse, mental health, and risk behaviors.
  19. Maintains the security of confidential documents.
  20. Maintains confidentiality at all times.
  21. Discusses any client information only with appropriate personnel when related to the care being provided, and ensures these conversations are not near any clients.
  22. Self-identifies potentially unsafe systems/processes/situations and takes initiative to report to the supervisor,
  23. Performs other duties and tasks as may be required or assigned.

Physical Demands:

  1. Stand or walk constantly (for up to an entire shift) on various surfaces (tile, concrete, carpet). Climb stairs, ramps, or ladders occasionally during shift.
  2. Must be able to kneel, squat, bend for any duration of time and run if needed.
  3. Occasionally bend/twist at waist/knees/neck to perform various duties, including lift or carry up to 80 lbs.
  4. Constant use of hands, arms and fingers in reaching/handling/grasping while using radio, phone, notepad, writing reports and other administrative tasks.

Requirements:

  1. Minimum high school diploma or equivalency
  2. Associates Degree in Social Services preferred
  3. Previous experience working with homeless persons.
  4. Strong ability to communicate with homeless individuals who are actively participating in substance abuse and other factors related to homelessness.
  5. Desire to work with homeless population.
  6. Bilingual (English/Spanish) required.
  7. Ability to assist with the collection of patient’s valuables.
  8. Experience handling confidential documents and detail-oriented.
  9. Ability to use email, database program(s) of agency and working knowledge of word processing (Microsoft Word) and spreadsheet programs.
  10. Ability to communicate clearly verbally and in writing
  11. Effective written and oral communication and interpersonal skills with ability to deal with all levels of personnel, general public and patients in a professional and effective manner; must be able to use initiative and independent judgment within established guidelines.
  12. Ability to assist with emergency and behavioral health personnel with aggressive patient situations.

Disclaimer: Salary offered will be based on the candidate’s relevant experience, qualifications, and in accordance with applicable laws and internal pay equity policies.

*All JWCH, Wesley Health Centers workforce members are recommended to be fully vaccinated and boosted against COVID-19.


Employee Benefits:

At JWCH Institute, Inc., we believe in taking care of those who take care of others. If you work 30+ hours per week, you’ll enjoy competitive pay and a robust benefits package that includes:

  • Medical, Dental, Vision
  • Monthly employer-sponsored allowance for assistance with health premiums.
  • Funded Health Savings Account (up to deductible) to assist with carrier-approved medical expenses.
  • Paid time off (vacation, sick leave) and 13 paid holidays.
  • 401(k) Safe Harbor Profit Sharing plan.
  • Mileage reimbursement.
  • Short- and long-term disability plans (LTD/STD).
  • Life insurance policy & AD&D, and more!

Become part of a team where your work matters. Apply today and help us change lives, one patient at a time.

JWCH Institute, Inc + Wesley Health Centers is an Equal Opportunity and Fair Chance Employer.

title: Electronics & ERS Student Placement (Powertrains)
description:
Red Bull Powertrains are offering multiple year-long placement opportunities within our Electronics & ERS Engineering Design teams. In these hands-on roles you will be emersed into the heart of our state-of-the-art Technical and Testing facilities where we drive engineering and innovation to the limit to develop cutting-edge Formula 1 power units. Pushing boundaries is in our DNA!

This placement opportunity will allow you to dive deep into the development process ERS Electronic components. Successful candidates will have a keen interest in one or more of the following areas: Electronic power conversion (DC/DC & DC/AC), high speed control electronics (Microcontroller & FPGA), sensor signal conditioning & measurement electronics (Amplifier, Filter & ADC), communication interfaces (e.g. Ethernet, CAN, FlexRay, SPI) and battery management systems.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Contribute to all stages of the engineering process from conceptual design, through manufacturing reviews, to live testing on our in-house state-of-the-art facilities
  • Applying engineering design principles using tools and techniques to develop real Power Unit components
  • Support the design, testing, and development of electronic components for the Energy Recovery System (ERS)
  • Assist with power electronics design, including high-power inverters, DC/DC converters and control circuits
  • Help build, test, and debug electronic components and systems
  • Contribute to the development and improvement of test rigs and software (e.g., LabVIEW, TestStand)
  • Create and update test procedures for electronic components
  • Analyse test data and assist with fault investigation to improve system reliability and performance
  • Prepare risk assessments and follow safety procedures to ensure a safe working environment
  • Interpreting and reporting data through technical documentation and presenting insights to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Collaborating closely with all the Technical and Testing teams to deliver world-class engineering solutions
  • Gaining direct exposure to the 2027 Formula 1 season and contributing to the future of Red Bull Powertrains

We’re looking for passionate, curious, and driven undergraduates who are eager to push the limits of engineering innovation in a fast paced, high-performance environment. If you're ready to take on real responsibility, solve real-world engineering challenges and contribute to the future of Red Bull Racing’s success on track, this is your opportunity.

Expected knowledge, experience & attributes of the successful candidates:

  • Knowledge and experience from at least one year of undergraduate study on either an electrical/ electronic engineering, mathematics or physics degree course
  • A solid understanding of engineering principles and the ability to apply mathematical methods to solve real-world problems
  • Familiarity with engineering software such as CAD, FEA, CFD, or system modelling (training will be provided)
  • Knowledge of electronic design and simulation tools (LTSpice or similar)
  • Design and layout of PCBs, including electronic circuit testing, debugging, and validation
  • Commissioning and troubleshooting of electronic systems and test rigs
  • Experience with handling and analysing data from simulations or physical tests and confidence in preparing high-quality technical documentation
  • Ability to break complex technical problems down to fundamental principles and understand the contributing physics
  • Ability to demonstrate a genuine passion for engineering through involvement in extra-curricular projects, previous placements, or work experience
  • Positive, can-do, attitude and willingness to learn new skills
  • Ability to follow best practice and work on multiple tasks simultaneously
  • Excellent communication skills and experience working in a team environment


The placement will be for 1 year, starting July 2027. To be considered for this Student Placement, please apply to this advert and submit both your CV and a one-page Cover Letter as two separate documents.


At Red Bull Powertrains, we believe that success isn’t just about speed, it’s about the team behind the victory. We trust, support, and challenge each other, always pushing for better. If you love solving complex problems, thinking fast, and making a real impact, this is the place for you. Alongside a competitive salary, you’ll enjoy:

  • Bonus scheme
  • Private healthcare
  • A pension scheme
  • On-site gym
  • Free daily food allowance
  • And many more!

Most importantly, you’ll play a key role in powering championship-winning cars. If you're ready to be part of something extraordinary, apply now and help shape the future of F1.

title: Child Psychiatrist | Regional Tertiary Hospital | North Queensland
description:
Consultant Psychiatrist – Child, Adolescent & Young Adult Services Regional Tertiary Public Health Service | North Queensland Total remuneration up to AUD $534,040 p.a. FTE (inclusive of incentives)

We are partnering with a large regional tertiary Hospital and Health Service delivering the full spectrum of public mental health care across a vast North Queensland catchment. Positions sit within an established Child, Adolescent and Young Adult mental health division based at a modern, purpose-built regional health campus, and are supported by an experienced multidisciplinary team, strong academic partnerships with a leading North Queensland university, and a network of 21 facilities spanning tertiary, regional, and remote outreach services.

The service provides complex secondary and tertiary psychiatric care to children, adolescents, and young adults across a comprehensive continuum, including:

  • Acute adolescent inpatient care
  • Community-based child and youth mental health teams
  • A dedicated regional adolescent forensic mental health service
  • An early intervention team focused on first-episode presentations and emerging serious mental illness

Your opportunity

  • Deliver expert consultant psychiatric care across acute inpatient, community, forensic, and early intervention settings
  • Rotate across teams aligned to your interests and expertise, or negotiate a stable primary attachment
  • Contribute to the clinical leadership, teaching, and supervision of registrars, trainees, and the multidisciplinary workforce
  • Engage in research and teaching through the service's university partnership
  • Support outreach into rural, remote, and Indigenous communities — a genuine draw for clinicians with an interest in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander mental health
  • Play an active role in shaping and expanding a growing regional CAYAS service
  • Positions available at Staff Specialist and Senior Staff Specialist level (L18–L27), dependent on experience

What's on offer

  • Total remuneration package up to AUD $534,040 p.a. FTE (inclusive of incentives)
  • Permanent full-time or part-time — hours genuinely negotiable
  • Employer superannuation contributions
  • Professional development allowance and leave
  • On-call and other award allowances
  • Generous annual and personal leave provisions
  • Queensland Health salary packaging with full FBT concessions (including novated leasing, meal and entertainment benefits, and remote area benefits where applicable)
  • Regional workforce incentives aligned to North Queensland classification
  • Attractive relocation support package for the right candidate
  • 482 and 494 visa sponsorship available for eligible international candidates
  • DAMA pathway applicable to this location — offering age concessions to 55, expanded occupation eligibility, and enhanced pathways to permanent residency

Requirements

  • Fellowship of the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists (FRANZCP) with completed or advanced training in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
  • Specialist registration, or eligibility for specialist registration, with the Medical Board of Australia
  • SIMGs with a "Substantially Comparable" RANZCP outcome are strongly encouraged to apply — our client is genuinely open to overseas-trained specialists and has a strong track record of supporting international clinicians through the specialist pathway
  • Current Class C driver's licence
  • Ability to meet Queensland Health credentialling and Scope of Clinical Practice requirements
  • Compliance with the service's Vaccine Preventable Disease screening and pre-employment check policies
  • A genuine interest in working within a regional, culturally diverse service environment

Life in North Queensland

North Queensland offers a genuine lifestyle proposition that is increasingly rare in metropolitan Australia — a vibrant coastal city set on a subtropical shoreline, framed by an offshore island and the Great Barrier Reef beyond. Cost of living and property are dramatically more affordable than Brisbane, Sydney, or Melbourne, and the city offers excellent public and private schooling, family-friendly communities, a growing café and dining scene, and one of the state's most highly regarded urban beaches. For clinicians with an interest in the outdoors, the region gives you the reef, tropical rainforest, and the Queensland outback all within easy reach — and Brisbane, Cairns, and Asia-Pacific destinations are all a short direct flight away. For international clinicians, the DAMA pathway makes this one of the strongest regions in Australia for genuine long-term residency planning.

title: Software Engineer 2 (Java / Kotlin) - Basket Building
description:

Allegro is home to 1,700+ tech experts, but our team? We are the driving force behind the Basket Building domain. We are designing and developing innovative solutions that help customers discover and easily use the best discounts during their shopping journey.

We are not just building standard features. We are inventing and creating a complex solution that hiper-personalizes offers for our buyers. By collaborating closely with ML specialists, we are building a tool that analyzes user preferences and cart contents in real-time to select the most relevant and attractive discounts, ensuring our customers always get the most value out of their shopping. If you love conceptual, greenfield work, want to leverage AI in your daily tasks, and prefer building from scratch over maintaining legacy code, you’re in the right place.

Important things for you:

    • Annual bonus based on your annual performance and company results.

What’s in it for you:

  • A 16" or 14" MacBook Pro or corresponding Dell with Windows (if you don't like Macs) and all the necessary accessories.
  • A wide selection of fringe benefits in a cafeteria plan - you choose what you like (e.g., medical, sports or lunch packages, insurance, purchase vouchers).

  • A training budget, inter-team tourism , hackathons, and an internal learning platform where you will find multiple trainings.

  • Social events for Allegro people - Spin Kilometers, Family Day, Fat Thursday, Advent of Code, and many other occasions we enjoy.

#goodtobehere means that:

  • You will join a team you can count on - we work with top-class specialists who have knowledge- and experience-sharing in their DNA.
  • You will love our level of autonomy in team organization, the space for continuous development, and the opportunity to try new things. You get to choose which technology solves the problem and you are responsible for what you create.
  • You will value our Developer Experience and the full platform of tools and technologies that make creating software easier. We rely on an internal ecosystem based on self-service and widely used tools such as Kubernetes, Docker, Consul, GitHub, and GitHub Actions. Thanks to this, you can contribute to Allegro from your very first days on the job.
  • You will be equipped with modern AI tools to automate repetitive tasks, allowing you to focus on developing new services and refining existing ones (also leveraging AI support).
  • You will create solutions that will be used (and loved!) by your friends, family and millions of our customers.
  • You will meet the Allegro Scale, which starts with over 1000 microservices, an open-source data bus (Hermes) with 300K+ rps, a Service Mesh with 1M+ rps, tens of petabytes of data, and production-used machine learning.

We create solutions we love (and can) to talk about!

Send us your CV and… see you at Allegro!

We are looking for people who:

  • Want to build tools that directly personalize the shopping experience, ensuring millions of users can seamlessly access the best deals and promos tailored to them.

  • Can collaborate effectively with ML experts to build complex tools that analyze historical data and shopping carts in real-time to make dynamic decisions.

title: Site Coördinator (ABT)
description:
Voor A.B.T. (Antwerp Bulk Terminal) - onze droge bulk divisie in de Antwerpse Haven - zijn we op zoek naar een Site Coördinator (m/v/x).

Functie

We zoeken een gemotiveerde collega met ambitie en doorgroeipotentieel. Je start in een ondersteunende rol met ruimte om je verder te ontwikkelen en op termijn door te groeien binnen ons technisch team.

De site coördinator is de link tussen de terminal en het technische management van de kaai en de vloer zelf. Je zorgt dat de wisselwerking tussen technische werken en de operaties vlot verloopt en dat de werkzaamheden op de terminal goed op elkaar zijn afgestemd.

Onder je verantwoordelijkheden valt de goede werking van de niet operationele machines (waterzuivering, poorten, verlichting etc) en de globale orde en netheid op de terminal door steeds de juiste teams aan te spreken.

Jouw taken omvatten oa:

  • Het zorgen voor een goede wisselwerking tussen alle werken op de terminal, zowel operationele werkzaamheden als interne en externe technische werken;

  • Het opvolgen van technische werkzaamheden en administratieve opvolging ervan;

  • Het zorgen voor een veilig onthaal en opvolging van de onderaannemers op de terminal;

  • Controleren van specifieke attesten(van onderaannemers), leveringen, kwaliteit van het werk van contractoren, leveranciers en/of dienstverleners, LOTO’s, bevoorrading;

  • Opvolgen van de algemene orde en netheid op de terminal en in die context de juiste mensen aan te sturen en werkaanvragen te doen;

  • Melden van defecten, incidenten en ongevallen volgens de juiste procedures;

  • Controleren van de werkzones op veilig werken en het correct uitvoeren van de werken;

  • Het opvolgen en aansturen van de waterzuiveringsinstallatie, lozingen en wekelijkse staalnames;

  • Het leiden van startwerkbesprekingen en uitreiken en opvolgen van werkvergunningen;

  • Coördineren en bijstaan bij het voorbereiden en veiligstellen van werkplaatsen (LOTO, product vrij etc);

  • De link vormen tussen operations en technische dienst zodat geplande onderhoudswerkzaamheden vlot en veilig verlopen met een minimale impact op de lopende operaties;

  • Je rapporteert aan de maintenance coördinator van de terminal.

Profiel

  • Je beschikt over een bachelor elektromechanica, facility management of gelijkwaardig door ervaring;

  • Je hebt een algemene brede technische kennis (mechanica, elektriciteit, …)

  • Je kan analytisch denken en je kan zelfstandig werken

  • Je kan planmatig, oplossingsgericht en georganiseerd werken

  • Je kan om met stressvolle situaties en je kan je flexibel opstellen binnen de organisatie

  • Je beschikt over goede communicatieve vaardigheden

  • Je kan zowel in groep als zelfstandig werken.

As Cluster Development Team Leader, you will play a pivotal role in shaping a place-based approach that maximises the economic benefits of offshore wind for Scotland’s ports, regional economies, communities, and supply chains.

This is a high-profile role, responsible for driving forward innovative place-based policy and aligning activity across government, industry, and public sector delivery partners to unlock private investment, accelerate regional growth, and ensure ports and associated infrastructure are positioned to capture long-term value. Reporting to the Head of Ports & Harbours Infrastructure and Community Benefits (C2), you will influence national policy, lead collaborative delivery, and help position Scotland as a global leader in offshore wind, with ports and place-based development at the heart of supply chain growth and the transition to net zero.

Overview of Directorate

The Offshore Wind Directorate leads on policy and programmes related to offshore renewables, marine energy and sectoral marine planning, to support the continued growth of the offshore wind sector.

The Directorate’s core aim is to maximise the significant economic benefits from the growth of offshore renewables for Scotland’s economy, citizens and environment as we transition to net zero. We also have a key role in ensuring the balance of economic and environmental objectives, with other users of the marine environment.

We support the development of Scotland’s offshore wind economy by:

  • working across the public sector to deploy strategic investment in ports and supply chain that grows our manufacturing base, attracting capital, inward investment, driving economic growth and job creation;
  • demonstrating the potential role for marine energy in Scotland’s low carbon energy system;
  • delivering enabling programmes e.g. through the Energy Act to streamline consenting, improve regulatory certainty, and accelerate deployment;
  • managing the constraints and opportunities of Scotland’s transition to net zero through the sustainable expansion of offshore renewables, enabled by sectoral marine planning that provides clarity, reduces risk, and supports balanced use of the marine space.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the development and delivery of a strategic offshore wind clustering approach, driving place-based activity that maximises investment, port infrastructure development, supply chain growth and economic impact.
  • Shape and implement innovative policy to support globally competitive offshore wind clusters, aligned with Scotland’s net zero and economic priorities.
  • Build and lead strategic partnerships across government, industry, and public sector partners to drive strong collaboration, deliver coordinated programmes and unlock shared opportunities.
  • Develop a coordinated approach to align public and private investment with clustering priorities, leveraging funding mechanisms and removing barriers to accelerate delivery and growth.
  • Work closely with the Offshore Wind Programme team and the Office of the Chief Economic Adviser to establish clear KPIs and measurable outcomes, supporting effective tracking of economic impact, inform decision-making, and drive continuous improvement.
  • Line management responsibility for one B3 and countersigning responsibility for one B2.

Experience

  1. Experience of policy development, policy delivery and working collaboratively with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders to influence outcomes and deliver shared objectives.
  2. Experience of leading high-performing teams, taking an agile approach to managing competing priorities and reactive demands while creating an inclusive environment and driving delivery at pace.
  3. Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex information clearly and concisely to a range of stakeholders at all levels, across both the public and private sectors.
  4. Experience of analysing a range of evidence and developing and presenting evidence-based recommendations to support/inform policy.
  5. Strong commercial awareness, applying an understanding of investment drivers and market dynamics to maximise economic outcomes and value for money.

Working pattern

This role is a permanent level transfer position.

This post is a full-time role, but we welcome applications from staff with different working patterns, proposed working patterns will be assessed against the business requirements for this post.

Our standard hours are 35 hours per week and we offer a range of flexible working options depending on the needs of the role, including Flexi-leave. Scottish Government staff in hybrid-compatible roles should aim to work in-person 40% of the time, either in an office or other agreed work location. If you have specific questions about the role you are applying for, please contact us.

How to Apply

Applications for this position will only be accepted from substantive C1 grade employees.

Please submit a statement outlining your suitability for the role, relevant skills and experience, and what you would bring to the team (maximum 500 words).

Vacancies close at 23:59pm on Tuesday 15 September.

If you have questions about your application please contact lorna.finlayson@gov.scot

Selection Process

All applicants will be invited to an informal discussion with the hiring manager. There will be no formal testing or assessment.

Discussions are expected to be scheduled for w/c TBC.

Recruitment Principles

As a government organisation, we adhere to the Civil Service Commission Recruitment Principles and we investigate any complaints received in relation to recruitment cases.

Apply before: 15/09/2026 (23:59)

title: Administrative Officer
description:
Administrative Officer
Salary: £25,000 per annum
Location: Based in Glasgow or Lanarkshire, with hybrid working arrangements and 2 days a week in the office
Contract/Hours: Permanent / Full Time – 35 hours per week

Closing date for applications is midnight of Sunday 20th September and interviews are provisionally scheduled for Tuesday 29th September


Benefits:

  • Over 7 weeks inclusive paid leave and the option to buy or sell leave
  • Excellent training and the opportunity to undertake professional training for some roles
  • Flexible maternity, paternity and adoption packages
  • Up to 5% employer contribution and life assurance cover
  • Blue Light Card eligibility with discounts at 15,000 national retailers
  • As part of our commitment to staff wellbeing, you’ll receive a paid annual Wellbeing Day to use however you choose, supporting a healthy balance between work and life.

At Action for Children, we offer more than just a job. Join us and you’ll be part of a team dedicated to giving children safe and happy childhoods. See how your skills can make a real difference, helping solve the problems children and young people face every day.

A bit about the role

As an Administrative Officer, you’ll be a valued member of our Business Support team based at the Scotland Head Office in Glasgow. Your work will ensure the Scotland Leadership Team receives high quality, reliable support — enabling them to guide and strengthen over 85 children, young people and family services across Scotland.

This is a varied and purposeful role where you’ll provide a wide range of administrative support to all members of the Scotland Leadership Team and across departments, building strong working relationships with colleagues and external partner agencies. You’ll act as the main contact for Scotland’s contract management process, ensuring all Children’s Services contracts are completed, signed off and returned.

Your responsibilities will also include supporting Operational Directors with diary management, collating and updating records on a monthly or quarterly basis, supporting all aspects of meeting admin including minute taking for operational and HR meetings, maintaining office supplies and services, reception cover, raising purchase orders, and following financial processes for invoice payments.

About the Service

Our Scotland Head Office provides central support to more than 85 Children’s Services across the country. These services work with children, young people and families in a wide range of settings, offering practical help, emotional support and specialist interventions. The Business Support team plays a crucial role in keeping these services running smoothly by ensuring leaders and practitioners have the information, resources and administrative support they need to deliver high‑quality, child‑centred practice.

What you do could make a difference

It’s a great opportunity to build your administrative experience while providing a valued support service to a friendly, welcoming team. You’ll be the first point of contact for internal and external visitors, helping everyone feel supported and ensuring they have a positive experience. It’s a role that brings real job satisfaction and a strong sense of purpose.

As an Administrative Officer, you’ll:

  • Bring a calm, professional and intuitive approach to your work, handling tasks with sensitivity and confidence.
  • Communicate clearly and warmly, always aiming to deliver an excellent standard of customer service.
  • Work efficiently and stay organised, meeting deadlines in a fast‑paced environment.
  • Show enthusiasm for learning new processes and share good practice with others.

Let’s talk about you

  • Business Administration S/NVQ is welcome but not essential — relevant experience is equally valued.
  • Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and the ability to work to tight deadlines.
  • Confident in taking responsibility for your own tasks and leading on specific pieces of work when required.
  • Skilled in using IT systems including SharePoint, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and bespoke databases.
  • Experience providing administrative support to senior managers, often managing competing priorities.
  • Fully committed to achieving the best outcomes for children and young people.
  • Able to handle confidential and sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.

Why Action for Children?

Every child should have a loving home, food, warmth, the chance to grow and learn - the support to cope with life’s challenges. But too many children don’t. By bringing your passion and unique skills and experience, you’ll help us change that where it really matters.

We've been driven by love to take action for children for over 150 years, giving them the protection and practical help they need. A lot’s changed since 1869. But what children really need, hasn’t. So as long as children need us, we’ll be here.

Will you join us?

Contact: Please submit an application via our careers page. If you have any further questions, you can contact Laura McCarthy at recruitmentservice@actionforchildren.org.uk quoting reference 13643

Diversity, equality and inclusion

We work hard to create an inclusive environment. One where individuality is celebrated and where everyone feels valued and supported. Because when we come together, with skills like yours, we’re capable of amazing things.

We actively encourage applications from people with Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic backgrounds and people with a disability, as these groups are under-represented within Action for Children.

title: Senior Finance Associate
description:
Position Title: Senior Finance Associate

Duty Station City: Caracas
Duty Station Country: Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela
Grade: G6
Contract Type: Special Short-Term
Recruiting Type: General Service
Vacancy Type: Special Vacancy Notice
Initial duration: until 31 december 2026

Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

Organizational Context and Scope

Under the overall supervision of the Resources Management Officer (RMO) in Caracas and direct supervision of the Finance and Administration Officer; and, in collaboration with relevant units in the Mission, the successful candidate will be responsible and accountable for supporting the resources management functions in the Mission.

• Provide overall support to the Resource Management Unit in activities related to monitoring, administrative, financial, procurement and other activities in accordance with IOM rules and regulations;
• Provide specialized advice and support to Project Managers and/or Head of Sub-office on financial and administrative matters;
• Provide support preparing annual budget submission and revisions including estimating the cost of staff as well as rental and utilities, office equipment and supplies, printing, and other contracts, services or running expenses;
• Assist in monitoring compliance with financial policies, procedures, rules and regulations;
• Consolidate data into financial statements and assist in monitoring expenditures to ensure they remain within authorized levels;
• Identify potential weaknesses on internal controls to safeguard the Organizations´s assets and propose corrective actions.
• Provide regular and ad hoc financial information to support informed financial decision making;
• Ensure that disbursements are made based on proper authorizations and supported by legitimate and sufficient documentation;
• Provide assistance responding to audit queries and follow up on audit recommendations;
• Review the status and monitor the proper maintenance of Vendor Accounts in accounting system;
• Assist in the preparation of budget, accounting, financial, statistical reports and other reports as required; and,
• Perform other related duties as required.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • High School diploma with six years of relevant experience; or,
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finances, or related field with four years of relevant professional experience.
  • Certified Public Accountant is an advantage
  • Knowledge of IPSAS is an advantage

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications e.g. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, E-mail, Outlook; previous experience in SAP is a distinct advantage;

  • Attention to detail, ability to organize paperwork in a methodical way;

  • Discreet, details and clients-oriented, patient and willingness to learn new things; and,

  • Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organization in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.

Skills

  • In depth knowledge of the broad range of migration related subject areas dealt with by the Organization; and,
  • Knowledge of UN and bilateral donor programming.
  • Knowledge of financial rules and regulations.

Languages

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in Spanish are mandatory. English is desirable.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.
  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.
  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.
  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.
  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings.

Notes

  • IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system

  • Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

  • Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

  • IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process.

  • This vacancy is only available for local citizens or foreigners with right of residence and right to work in the country.

  • For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Onderzoeker veiligheid en recht
description:
Kom jij bij het CBS statistiek maken over belangrijke, complexe thema’s als strafrecht?

Ben je breed geïnteresseerd en wil je vanuit maatschappelijk belang bijdragen met jouw werk? Solliciteer dan nu!

Waar jij het verschil maakt

  • Je bent als onderzoeker van de statistieken vervolging en berechting, en gevangeniswezen verantwoordelijk voor de jaarlijkse statistiekproductie. Je bent het aanspreekpunt voor vragen over het gebruik van deze data en bent de inhoudelijke expert op dit gebied.

  • Je vertegenwoordigt het CBS op operationeel en tactisch niveau in contacten met data leveranciers.

  • Je werkt mee aan de halfjaarlijkse jeugdbescherming en -reclasseringcyclus en ontwikkelt je als/tot expert op dit terrein. Dit is een onderdeel van het Beleidsinformatie Jeugdproject.

  • Je koppelt bestanden, doet plausibiliteitscontroles en bouwt outputtabellen.

  • Je houdt oog voor procesverbeteringen in al bestaande processen.

  • Je denkt mee over eventuele verdieping of verbreding binnen de onderwerp in het sociaal domein.

  • Je hebt brede interesses en je ziet een project over een ander onderwerp in het sociaal domein als een leuke uitdaging.

  • Je ziet cijfers niet alleen als een uitkomst van een technisch proces. Je kunt ze echt doorgronden en verbanden leggen.

Je toekomstige collega's

Je komt te werken in het team Rechtsbescherming en veiligheid. Hier maken we met een team van 20 enthousiaste onderzoekers en projectleiders cijfers over rechtsbescherming en veiligheid. Denk aan cijfers over asiel en geregistreerde criminaliteit. We brengen de hele strafrechtketen in kaart, van verdachten tot gevangenen.
Een groot deel van het werkpakket van het team bestaat uit aanvullende statistische dienstverlening, in opdracht van ministeries:

  • Beleidsinformatie Jeugd, waar we vanuit ons team de jeugdbescherming en -reclassering in beeld brengen.

  • Cohortonderzoeken over asiel en inburgering,

  • Samenwerkingen op het terrein van cijfers over criminaliteit, zoals zicht op ondermijning en informatie analyseteam.

Team Rechtsbescherming en veiligheid is onderdeel van de directie met statistieken over de quartaire sector. We zoeken binnen de sector steeds vaker de connectie tussen de teams. Zo stemmen we interesses en ontwikkelwensen zo goed mogelijk af op projectambities.

Dit ben jij

  • Je hebt een academisch werk- en -denkniveau en hebt minimaal twee jaar ervaring in eenzelfde soort functie.

  • Je moet de complexiteit in de strafrechtketen goed kennen.

  • Je kunt werken met R; bijna al onze processen zijn namelijk met R gebouwd.

  • Je hebt een brede interesse en je kunt meepraten over andere onderwerpen, zoals sociaal domein.

  • Je werkt secuur en zelfstandig, kunt opbouwende feedback geven en ontvangen.

Feitelijk goed geregeld

Voor onze arbeidsvoorwaarden volgen wij de CAO Rijk. Dat betekent dat je onder andere kunt rekenen op het volgende:

  • Een salaris van minimaal € 3.496,- en maximaal € 6.275,- bruto per maand op basis van 36 uur. Afhankelijk van je kennis en ervaring.

  • 8% vakantiegeld en een 13e maand. In totaal is dit 16,5% bovenop je salaris. Dit noemen wij het Individueel Keuze Budget (IKB). Je bepaalt zelf hoe, wanneer en op welke manier je dit budget wilt inzetten.

  • Pensioenopbouw bij het ABP Pensioenfonds.

  • Een laptop (Microsoft of Apple) en mobiele telefoon (Android of iOS).

  • Twee tot drie dagen thuiswerken, de rest ben je aanwezig in ons onlangs gerenoveerde gebouw. In je team maak je daar verder afspraken over.

Kom werken aan de feiten

We sluiten de vacature op zondag 20 september.

De selectie vindt plaats in de week van maandag 21 september.

title: Supervisor Process Engineering
description:
The Company

Dexcom Corporation (NASDAQ DXCM) is a pioneer and global leader in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Dexcom began as a small company with a big dream: To forever change how diabetes is managed. To unlock information and insights that drive better health outcomes. Here we are 25 years later, having pioneered an industry. And we're just getting started. We are broadening our vision beyond diabetes to empower people to take control of health. That means personalized, actionable insights aimed at solving important health challenges. To continue what we've started: Improving human health.

We are driven by thousands of ambitious, passionate people worldwide who are willing to fight like warriors to earn the trust of our customers by listening, serving with integrity, thinking big, and being dependable. We've already changed millions of lives and we're ready to change millions more. Our future ambition is to become a leading consumer health technology company while continuing to develop solutions for serious health conditions. title: Clinical Director & Staff Specialist - Psychiatrist
location: Central Coast, New South Wales, Australia
description:
Clinical Director & Staff Specialist – Mental Health Public Local Health District

We are currently partnering with a well-established NSW public Local Health District to recruit an experienced Consultant Psychiatrist into a combined Clinical Director and Staff Specialist appointment within its Mental Health Service. This is a rare opportunity to take on genuine service leadership within a growing coastal district health service, while maintaining a rewarding clinical caseload.

About the service

Our client is a NSW Health Local Health District serving one of the state's fastest-growing coastal populations, located within easy reach of Sydney. The Mental Health Service provides a comprehensive continuum of care — spanning acute inpatient, community, consultation-liaison, older persons, youth, and specialist mental health programs — across two major public hospitals and a network of community mental health centres. The service is supported by a well-established multidisciplinary workforce and is investing significantly in workforce development, service redesign, and integrated models of care to meet the demands of a rapidly expanding catchment.

Your opportunity

  • Provide clinical and strategic leadership across the district's Mental Health Service in a dedicated Clinical Director capacity
  • Contribute to clinical governance, service planning, quality improvement, and workforce development initiatives
  • Maintain a Staff Specialist clinical caseload aligned with your sub-specialty interest and service need
  • Lead, mentor, supervise and support consultant colleagues, trainees, JMOs and multidisciplinary staff
  • Partner closely with the Director of Mental Health, executive, and cross-directorate colleagues on the strategic direction of the service
  • Represent the service in inter-agency, LHD, and state-wide forums as required
  • Contribute to teaching, training and research activities, with links available to affiliated universities

What's on offer

  • Salary and conditions in accordance with the NSW Staff Specialist (State) Award Determination
  • Level of appointment negotiated based on experience and expertise
  • Employer superannuation contributions
  • Private Practice Arrangements available under the NSW model
  • Professional development leave and allowance
  • Generous annual leave provisions
  • NSW Health salary packaging — including options for novated leasing, meal and entertainment benefits, and remote area housing benefits where applicable
  • Attractive relocation support may be negotiated for the right candidate
  • Visa sponsorship available for eligible international candidates
  • Genuine flexibility around clinical, leadership and academic components of the role

Requirements

  • Fellowship of the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists (FRANZCP)
  • Specialist registration, or eligibility for specialist registration, with AHPRA as a Psychiatrist
  • Demonstrated leadership experience within a public mental health service or comparable setting
  • Strong track record in clinical governance, service development, and multidisciplinary team leadership
  • SIMGs already on an approved RANZCP specialist pathway are welcome to apply
  • Australian working rights, or eligibility for employer-sponsored visa
  • Current National Police Check and compliance with NSW Health immunisation and screening requirements
  • Commitment to the values of EEO, WHS, ethical practice, cultural safety, and the NSW Health Code of Conduct

Life on the Central Coast

The Central Coast is one of NSW's most sought-after lifestyle regions — a string of relaxed beachside communities set between long stretches of surf coast, national parks, and calm coastal lakes. Property is dramatically more affordable than Sydney or the Northern Beaches, and the region offers excellent public and private schooling, family-friendly neighbourhoods, and a strong sense of community. Sydney's CBD is a straightforward train or drive south, so you can enjoy genuine coastal living without giving up easy access to a global city, its airport, or its cultural offerings. For families, active professionals, and clinicians seeking a sustainable long-term career base outside a capital city, few Australian regions offer a better balance.

title: APAC Pricing Specialist
description:
Pricing Analysis & Simulation

  • Prepare pricing analysis, market comparisons, price-ratio checks and value-chain review materials to support pricing decisions.

  • Support pricing simulations, scenario analysis and impact assessment for price adjustments, price-list releases and market deployment.

  • Analyze pricing realization, margin movement, leakage, abnormal discounting and corridor deviation based on available business data.

  • Translate pricing data into clear analytical outputs, dashboards and management-ready summaries.

Price List & Release Support

  • Support preparation and maintenance of pricing master files, release working files and pricing review trackers.

  • Prepare release support materials, including price-list comparison, exception tracking, approval evidence and implementation status.

  • Coordinate publication-readiness inputs with Product Information & Intelligence as guided by the APAC Pricing Manager.

  • Maintain clean documentation of pricing assumptions, input files, review comments, release versions and follow-up actions.

Pricing Realization Tracking

  • Track pricing realization after release and prepare realization reports for APAC Pricing Manager review.

  • Monitor price implementation, market feedback, deviation cases and pricing-effectiveness indicators.

  • Support next-cycle refinement by collecting evidence, summarizing findings and preparing improvement recommendations.

  • Maintain follow-up discipline on pricing actions, owner updates, evidence gates and implementation progress.

Pricing Data & Tool Discipline

  • Maintain structured pricing datasets and working files with clear version control and data-quality discipline.

  • Support pricing dashboards, Excel models, Power BI views and other analytical tools used in pricing reviews.

Education & Background

  • Bachelor’s degree or above in Economics, Finance, Business, Statistics, Data Analytics, Engineering, Mathematics or a related discipline.

  • Relevant internship or work experience in pricing, business analysis, commercial analysis, revenue management, product analytics or market research is preferred.

  • Automotive, industrial products, consumer goods or multi-country business exposure is a plus but not required.

Core Capabilities

  • Strong analytical and quantitative capability; able to work with structured data and identify patterns, exceptions and business implications.

  • Advanced Excel capability, including large workbook management, formulas, pivot tables and structured model maintenance.

  • Power BI, Python, SQL / MySQL, VBA, R or equivalent analytical tools are strong advantages.

  • Ability to prepare clear pricing analysis, dashboards, summaries and business-facing reports.

  • Good understanding of pricing, profitability, margin, discount, channel economics or business-performance concepts.

  • Detail-oriented, disciplined with data quality, and comfortable working with version control and working-file ownership.

  • Strong communication skills in English; additional APAC language capability is a plus.
